title: Scoped prefetch vs lazy-load — econ portrait (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft that compares two operational strategies for reducing per-token cost and tail latency under sessionized conversational workloads: (A) scoped prefetch (intent-aware prefetch of likely KV prefixes + soft prewarm) and (B) lazy-load (on-demand KV population + opportunistic batching). The doc shows microbench results, cost math per 10k sessions, and quick guidance for product routes where either strategy makes sense.

Summary (short):
- Scoped prefetch reduces cold-start p99s and increases KV hit-rate at the cost of extra wasted compute for mispredicted prefixes. Works best for predictable session patterns (assistant/chatbot, known prompt templates).
- Lazy-load minimizes wasted work and is cheap at low session density, but suffers higher tail latency under microbursts and high churn.
- A hybrid with short prefetch horizon + adaptive cancel yields ~80% of prefetch p99 improvements at 40% of the extra cost (in our bench).

Methodology (test harness):
- Models: small-chat (7B opt-style), mid-chat (13B decoder-only), long-context variant (13B w/ 32k tokens KV).
- Hardware: A100s (40GB) for small/mid, H100 for long-context runs.
- Workload: sessionized arrivals with Zipf alpha=1.1 for prompt variety; 10k synthetic sessions; inter-arrival distributions: steady (Poisson, lambda=30s), microburst (peak 500 concurrent), and churn (sessions created/destroyed frequently).
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency for first token and full-response; per-1k-session cost (GPU-seconds converted using $/GPU-hr calibrated to internal committed pricing); KV hit-rate; wasted-prefetch-ratio (prefetched tokens later unused).
- Batching: continuous batching with 10ms harvest window for both strategies unless otherwise noted.

Configuration knobs defined:
- Prefetch window: number of tokens predicted to be needed ahead (0, 64, 256).
- Prediction model: light classifier (session metadata + recent history) with 72% macro accuracy in bench.
- Lazy-load threshold: defer KV population until first response generation op (default).
- Hybrid: prefetch 64 tokens if classifier confidence > 0.6; cancel prefetch if session idle > 500ms.

Representative numeric results (aggregated across models and weighted by session length) — note: these are bench sketches, not product SLA numbers:

Table: latency (ms) and cost ($) per 10k sessions

Mode                 | first-token p50 | first-token p95 | first-token p99 | avg cost /10k sessions
---------------------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|------------------------
Scoped-prefetch-256  | 28              | 64              | 210             | 1,820                 
Scoped-prefetch-64   | 32              | 78              | 260             | 1,560                 
Hybrid-prefetch-64   | 36              | 93              | 290             | 1,230                 
Lazy-load (baseline)  | 45              | 180             | 640             | 980                   

Observations from table:
- Prefetch always leads to lower p50/p95; improvements at p99 are largest for sessions with repeated context where KV hits are high.
- Cost increases for prefetch correlate strongly with misprediction rate and prefetch horizon. Prefetch-256 wasted cycles were visible in churn workload.
- Hybrid gives most latency upside while capping incremental cost. In our sweep hybrid reduced p99 by ~55% vs lazy-load while increasing cost by ~25%.

KV hit-rate and wasted work (example breakdown)
- Lazy-load: effective KV hit-rate = 0.42 (only after first generation). Wasted work N/A.
- Prefetch-64: hit-rate = 0.71; wasted-prefetch-ratio = 0.18 (prefetched tokens not consumed).
- Prefetch-256: hit-rate = 0.78; wasted-prefetch-ratio = 0.36 (more aggressive horizon).
- Hybrid-prefetch-64: hit-rate = 0.68; wasted=0.09 (cancels and confidence gating help).

Burst behavior (microburst scenario):
- At peak concurrency, lazy-load p99 spikes to >1.2s due to KV population contention and cache fill pressure. Prefetch modes keep fast-path cache primed and reduce burst p99 to 200–400ms depending on horizon.
- When prefetch misprediction is high (highly diverse sessions) prefetch creates short-lived KV eviction pressure; observing this requires larger cache sizes or smarter eviction.

Cost modeling (approx):
- Cost = base-serving + prefetch-overhead - amortized-savings-from-higher-throughput.
- Example math (prefetch-64): additional GPU work per prefetch = 0.35 GPU-seconds; with 10k sessions and 0.18 wasted fraction -> extra 630 GPU-seconds -> at $3.0/GPU-hr internal rate = $5.25 incremental. But latency savings can enable smaller instance count and lower tail-SLO penalties (hard to express as simple $).

ASCII chart: p99 latency vs KV hit-rate (prefetch-64)

KV-hit | p99 (ms)
-------|---------
0.2    | 780
0.4    | 420
0.6    | 310
0.8    | 205
0.95   | 160

Decision guidance (draft):
- Use scoped prefetch (64 token horizon) for assistant/chat routes with predictable templates, long-lived sessions (>3 turns), and tight p99 targets. Accept a 10–40% cost increase for predictable UX win.
- Use lazy-load for low-volume, exploratory routes (search-augmented Q&A, ephemeral form assistants) where wasted prefetch dominates.
- Try hybrid approach for mid-volume routes where traffic is bursty but has moderate predictability: set classifier confidence threshold and short cancel timeout.

Implementation concerns & ops notes:
- Prefetch cancellation needs to be supported at runtime to avoid excess queueing; implement circuit breaker to drop low-confidence prefetch on high CPU/GPU pressure.
- Observability: add a prefetch_trace_id and expose per-request prefetch state in traces; add short-lived metric for wasted_prefetch_ratio and prefetch_cancel_rate.
- Memory: aggressive prefetch increases KV occupancy; work with platform to reserve a prefetch partition or tune eviction to avoid thrash.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Repeat bench on G5/H100 configuration (we only ran A100/H100 mix).
- Sweep classifier thresholds more finely (0.5,0.6,0.7) and measure SLO vs cost inflection.
- Measure interaction with larger batching windows (20ms) — could change relative benefit.
- Add user-facing latency proxies (roundtrip + network) to map bench numbers to UX.

Notes to self (rough):
- Share with Platform (Mei) to validate eviction manifest.
- Follow up on JIRA-OBS-910 for adding prefetch metrics to tracing.
- Put a one-pager for PMs summarizing UX tradeoffs (short bullets + recommended defaults).

Appendix: short raw timeseries snapshot (sample run, 10k sessions, microburst)
- Lazy-load: median first-token 46ms; p95=192ms; p99=0.64s; cost=980
- Prefetch-64: median 34ms; p95=76ms; p99=270ms; cost=1560
- Hybrid-64: median 39ms; p95=88ms; p99=300ms; cost=1230

End of draft.
